subject: Security review kickoff & scope clarification - Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acmehealth.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@acmehealth.com>, Rajesh Kulkarni <rajesh.k@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Security review kickoff: Acme Health

Hi Laura / Emily / Rajesh —

Great to meet during the discovery call earlier. Per our conversation, we'd like to kick off the formal security review so your security/procurement team can validate Redwood's controls and determine systems in scope. To make this efficient, can you confirm the following items for us before the kickoff meeting?

- Which deployment mode are you evaluating (Redwood hosted API vs Redwood Private/VPC)?
- Will Acme be sending or storing any regulated data (PHI, PCI, or other high-sensitivity PII)?
- Primary procurement/legal contact for contract & data processing terms (if different from Rajesh).
- Target timeline for completion (internal deadlines, procurement windows).
- Any existing questionnaire you prefer us to fill (or attach) — otherwise we can intake via the attached summary and a short Q/A session.

I've attached a short Redwood_Security_Summary.pdf that covers SOC 2, encryption, and deployment options. If you already have a questionnaire, please send it over and we'll prioritize intake.

Proposed next steps:
1) You send any formal questionnaire or required evidence list.
2) We intake and assign an SE + Security lead to the case (cc'ing internal folks shortly).
3) Kickoff call to review scope and timeline (~30–45m).

Proposed kickoff windows next week: Mon 6/29 10:00am PT or Tue 6/30 9:00am PT. What works best?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap. We're ready to start the security intake. I'm attaching our standard Acme_Security_Questionnaire_v1.docx — please complete the sections for vendor controls and return.

To answer the quick items:
- We expect to evaluate both Redwood hosted API (initial PoC) and Redwood Private for production.
- The workload will include PHI (limited patient identifiers) in a subset of requests — will need HIPAA considerations.
- Procurement contact: Rajesh Kulkarni (cc'd). Legal will loop in separately if needed.
- Target timeline: procurement wants vendor review completed by mid-July to align with a July pilot.

We can do Mon 6/29 10:00am PT for kickoff. Please loop in your security lead and SE.

Confirmed kickoff: Mon 6/29 10:00am PT. Agenda we'll cover: scope (systems in/out), review questionnaire intake path, evidence expectations (attestations, config screenshots, network diagrams), timeline and next milestones.

Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Technical clarifications ahead of kickoff

Hi all —

A few quick technical questions so we can prepare the right evidence for the kickoff:

1) For the PoC, will Acme route traffic to Redwood's hosted API or do you plan to deploy Redwood Private/VPC from day one? If hosted, do you have data residency requirements (US-only region)?
2) For PHI handling: will PHI be sent in raw request bodies, or will requests be tokenized/masked on the client prior to call? Any example traffic profiles (req/sec, avg tokens per req, peak TPS) would help us size the evidence and recommend a deployment model.
3) Do you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in production, or will Redwood-managed encryption be acceptable initially?

If you can drop short answers here, we'll prepare the completed questionnaire sections and the network/topology diagram for the kickoff.

Thanks — Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement requirements / evidence requests

Marissa / team —

From procurement/legal side, to keep things moving we need the following items included in the evidence bundle:

- SOC 2 Type II attestation and date (or SOC 2 report access instructions)
- List of third-party subprocessors and subvendors
- Encryption at rest and in transit technical details (algorithms / TLS versions supported)
- Data retention and deletion policy for logs and request data (how long, how to request deletion)
- Incident notification SLA and contact for security events
- Network architecture diagram showing where customer data resides and any cross-region flows

If you can provide a network diagram and the SOC doc ahead of the kickoff that will help Procurement triage the vendor quickly. We also have a short procurement checklist we can share if helpful.

Thanks,
Rajesh Kulkarni
Senior Procurement Manager | Acme Health
rajesh.k@acmehealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rajesh Kulkarni <rajesh.k@acmehealth.com>, Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@acmehealth.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Procurement requirements / evidence requests

Rajesh —

Thanks — quick answers and links below; we'll assemble a packaged evidence bundle (attestations, screenshots, network diagram) and upload by EOD 7/2 as discussed.

- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II (covering security & availability) with period ending 2025-11-30. We will provide the report under NDA; instructions/portal link: https://redwood.app/security/soc2-access
- Subprocessors: List included in the evidence bundle (standard SaaS vendor list + cloud infra providers).
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; TLS 1.2+ for in-transit; we support TLS 1.3. More details in the bundle.
- Data retention: Default request logs retained 30 days; audit logs retained 365 days. We can provide custom retention and deletion APIs for Private customers. Details and deletion request process in the evidence bundle.
- Incident notification: We commit to 1-hour initial notification for sev-1 incidents and regular updates per the incident response SLA.
- Network diagram: attaching network-diagram.png showing hosted vs VPC topology and data flow.

To Rajesh's point on KMS: for Redwood Hosted we offer managed encryption keys by default; we also support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private deployments. We'll call this out in the evidence package.

Next steps:
- We'll upload the evidence bundle (SOC access instructions, subprocessors list, encryption matrix, screenshots, network diagram) to the HubSpot/secure share by EOD 2026-07-02.
- Kickoff remains Mon 6/29 10:00am PT to walk through the questionnaire and scope.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
